choices.text: Because the roots eat the food before it reaches the soil
They do not eat at all: roots drink water and minerals, and the leaves make the food with sunlight
Because there is no water in the soil

questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food. Reteach point: Roots drink water and minerals; the leaves make the food with sunlight. The plant does not eat food like we do. Check scene s4: watch what the roots really take in, and what the leaves do with sunlight.
questions.misconception: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food.
questions.prompt: Why do plants NOT take food from the soil through their roots?

questions.feedback: Scenes s1 and s2 fix the order: the roots drink the water, the stem carries it up, and it arrives at the leaves.
questions.prompt: Name, in order, the three parts of the plant that water passes through on its journey from the soil to the leaves.

choices.text: It makes the food for the plant
It holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves
It drinks water from the soil

questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes the picture: the stem is the lift and the road - it holds the plant up and water travels up it from the roots to the leaves.
questions.prompt: What does the stem do for the plant?

questions.answer: Sunlight and water, which the roots drink and the stem carries up.
questions.feedback: Scene s3 fixes the method: the leaves catch sunlight and use it with water to make food - the plant makes its food instead of eating it.
questions.prompt: What do the leaves use to make food for the plant?
